COCO_detection_JSON.mmdetection_compatibility: native (CocoDataset, no custom dataset class needed)
COCO_detection_JSON.negative_image_support: first-class: an image may appear in `images` with zero entries in `annotations`; requires filter_empty_gt=False so the 500 No Finding negatives are retained
COCO_detection_JSON.category_metadata_support: explicit and extensible; can carry canonical_class_id and class_id_original alongside the contiguous COCO category_id
COCO_detection_JSON.bbox_format: [x, y, width, height] absolute pixels; direct, lossless map from canonical xyxy_original_image (w = x_max - x_min, h = y_max - y_min)
COCO_detection_JSON.bbox_coordinate_fidelity: absolute pixels; no normalization, no precision loss
COCO_detection_JSON.traceability: annotation objects accept extra keys: canonical_ann_id, source_row_id, original_image_id, rad_id
COCO_detection_JSON.ssod_compatibility: strong: teacher-student SSOD implementations in MMDetection consume COCO; unlabeled/negative images fit the same schema
COCO_detection_JSON.pseudo_label_output_compatibility: pseudo-labels can be emitted directly as COCO annotations, reusing the same categories and evaluation path
COCO_detection_JSON.fit_for_this_thesis: best preserves the image-level negative vs detection-category separation this thesis depends on
COCO_detection_JSON.selection_reason: Native MMDetection/Detectron2 fit; first-class support for zero-annotation negative images; standard COCO mAP@0.5:0.95 via pycocotools; explicit categories; supports traceability fields back to the canonical schema.

YOLO_txt.mmdetection_compatibility: weak (requires conversion or a custom dataset)
YOLO_txt.coco_map_compatibility: indirect (must convert back to COCO for pycocotools mAP)
YOLO_txt.negative_image_support: fragile: negatives are represented by an EMPTY .txt file (or a missing file); silent-drop risk for the 500 No Finding images
YOLO_txt.multi_class_support: yes, but classes are bare integer indices
YOLO_txt.category_metadata_support: minimal: class names live in a separate side file; no room for canonical/original id metadata
YOLO_txt.bbox_format: normalized center-based (cx, cy, w, h in [0,1]); requires a lossy round-trip from canonical xyxy_original_image
YOLO_txt.bbox_coordinate_fidelity: reduced: normalization introduces float rounding and depends on exact image dimensions; conversion risk from the canonical absolute xyxy
YOLO_txt.traceability: none in-format; would need an external side-car mapping
YOLO_txt.ssod_compatibility: possible in YOLO-native SSOD, but off-stack for MMDetection
YOLO_txt.pseudo_label_output_compatibility: would need conversion back to COCO for evaluation, adding a second lossy hop
YOLO_txt.reproducibility_ecosystem: popular but tied to the YOLO ecosystem
YOLO_txt.fit_for_this_thesis: poor: the negative-image representation is exactly the part this thesis cannot afford to get wrong
YOLO_txt.rejection_reason: Normalized center-based bbox adds conversion risk from canonical xyxy_original_image; negative images are represented by empty txt files, which is fragile here; weaker fit for MMDetection and the COCO mAP pipeline.

Pascal_VOC_XML.mmdetection_compatibility: supported but legacy (VOCDataset); off the COCO path
Pascal_VOC_XML.coco_map_compatibility: poor: VOC-style AP differs from COCO mAP@0.5:0.95; conversion needed
Pascal_VOC_XML.negative_image_support: unclean: an object-less XML must still exist per negative image; less explicit than COCO's images-without-annotations
Pascal_VOC_XML.category_metadata_support: implicit only; no central category table
Pascal_VOC_XML.bbox_coordinate_fidelity: good: absolute pixels, matches canonical xyxy
Pascal_VOC_XML.traceability: would require non-standard custom XML tags
Pascal_VOC_XML.ssod_compatibility: weak; modern SSOD tooling assumes COCO
Pascal_VOC_XML.pseudo_label_output_compatibility: awkward: one XML file per pseudo-labelled image per iteration
Pascal_VOC_XML.reproducibility_ecosystem: dated; less tooling for COCO-style evaluation
Pascal_VOC_XML.fit_for_this_thesis: poor: 4,894 separate XML files and a non-COCO AP definition work against the locked mAP@0.5:0.95 metric
Pascal_VOC_XML.rejection_reason: One XML per image is cumbersome for 4,894 controlled-scope images; less suitable for COCO-style mAP@0.5:0.95 and modern MMDetection workflows; negative images are represented less cleanly than in COCO.

JSONL_custom.mmdetection_compatibility: none out of the box; requires a custom dataset class
JSONL_custom.coco_map_compatibility: requires a custom evaluator or a conversion to COCO
JSONL_custom.bbox_coordinate_fidelity: can be perfect, but the guarantee is ours to maintain
JSONL_custom.traceability: excellent in principle (any field can be carried)
JSONL_custom.reproducibility_ecosystem: weakest: bespoke format means results are harder for others to reproduce or compare
JSONL_custom.implementation_risk: high: custom dataset + custom evaluator are new surfaces for silent bugs in the very metric the thesis reports
JSONL_custom.fit_for_this_thesis: poor: flexibility does not compensate for hand-rolled evaluation code on the primary metric
JSONL_custom.rejection_reason: Non-standard; would require a custom dataset and evaluator; higher reproducibility risk; weak fit for MMDetection/SSOD without extra custom code.

format_comparison_conclusion: COCO is selected not merely because it is common, but because it best preserves the required separation between image-level negatives and detection categories, supports standard COCO mAP evaluation, and minimizes custom evaluation code in the later MMDetection/SSOD pipeline.

MMDetection.object_detection_support: native: modular PyTorch detection toolbox with a large model zoo (Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, DINO, etc.)
MMDetection.coco_dataset_compatibility: native CocoDataset; no custom dataset class needed
MMDetection.coco_map_compatibility: native CocoMetric via pycocotools; mAP@0.5:0.95 out of the box
MMDetection.ssod_teacher_student_readiness: official semi-supervised components (e.g. SoftTeacher / MeanTeacher-style hooks, EMA teacher); teacher-student SSOD is a documented use case
MMDetection.labeled_unlabeled_pipeline_support: official multi-branch pipeline and semi-supervised dataloader for labeled/unlabeled dataset preparation
MMDetection.config_reproducibility: config-driven training; the full experiment is captured in a versionable config file
MMDetection.empty_no_finding_image_handling: supported via filter_empty_gt=False; the 500 No Finding negatives are retained rather than silently dropped
MMDetection.dicom_loader_extensibility: transform/pipeline registry allows a custom DICOM LoadImage transform without forking the framework
MMDetection.pseudo_label_workflow: pseudo-labels flow through the same COCO-shaped structures used for training and evaluation
MMDetection.classwise_ap_ap50_ap75_readiness: CocoMetric reports AP50, AP75 and per-class AP without custom code
MMDetection.implementation_burden: low-medium: mostly configuration, little bespoke code
MMDetection.research_reproducibility: high: config + seed + published baselines make results comparable
MMDetection.fit_for_this_thesis: direct match: COCO detection + COCO mAP + teacher-student SSOD + labeled/unlabeled handling + config reproducibility
MMDetection.selection_reason: Modular PyTorch-based detection toolbox with native COCO dataset and COCO-style evaluation; official semi-supervised object detection components (labeled/unlabeled dataset preparation, multi-branch pipeline, semi-supervised dataloader, teacher-student / MeanTeacher-style training); config-driven training suits reproducibility. Best fit for a teacher-student SSOD thesis pipeline.

Detectron2_optional.coco_dataset_compatibility: strong: COCO and custom dataset registration
Detectron2_optional.ssod_teacher_student_readiness: no first-party SSOD components; teacher-student would rely on external repos (e.g. Unbiased Teacher) or bespoke implementation
Detectron2_optional.labeled_unlabeled_pipeline_support: no official labeled/unlabeled multi-branch dataloader; would need custom plumbing
Detectron2_optional.empty_no_finding_image_handling: supported, but requires care with filter_empty_annotations to keep negatives
Detectron2_optional.pseudo_label_workflow: would need a custom pseudo-label loop and EMA teacher
Detectron2_optional.implementation_burden: medium-high for SSOD: the semi-supervised layer must be built for this project
Detectron2_optional.research_reproducibility: good, but SSOD code would be project-specific
Detectron2_optional.fit_for_this_thesis: adequate as a detection backbone, weaker as an SSOD platform without extra custom work
Detectron2_optional.rejection_reason: Strong PyTorch detection framework with good COCO/custom dataset support and a suitable fallback if MMDetection setup fails; however the teacher-student SSOD pipeline would require more custom implementation in this project. Retained as fallback only, and only after GPT re-review.

YOLO_based_framework.object_detection_support: native and fast; strong single-stage baselines
YOLO_based_framework.coco_dataset_compatibility: indirect: expects YOLO-native layout; COCO must be converted, which conflicts with the COCO-master source of truth
YOLO_based_framework.coco_map_compatibility: reports its own mAP; alignment with pycocotools mAP@0.5:0.95 requires care/conversion
YOLO_based_framework.ssod_teacher_student_readiness: SSOD exists in the YOLO ecosystem but is not aligned with the planned MMDetection SSOD protocol
YOLO_based_framework.labeled_unlabeled_pipeline_support: not first-class for the planned labeled/unlabeled COCO protocol
YOLO_based_framework.empty_no_finding_image_handling: risky: negatives are expressed as empty label files; silent-drop risk for the 500 No Finding images
YOLO_based_framework.dicom_loader_extensibility: possible but off the framework's standard path
YOLO_based_framework.pseudo_label_workflow: YOLO-native; would diverge from the COCO master
YOLO_based_framework.classwise_ap_ap50_ap75_readiness: available, but under the framework's own metric implementation rather than pycocotools
YOLO_based_framework.implementation_burden: medium: easy to train, but the SSOD + COCO + negative-image protocol must be re-adapted
YOLO_based_framework.research_reproducibility: good, but tied to a different evaluation stack
YOLO_based_framework.fit_for_this_thesis: poor as primary: the annotation and evaluation pipeline is YOLO-native and diverges from the locked COCO/MMDetection protocol
YOLO_based_framework.rejection_reason: Easy to train and deploy with a strong baseline ecosystem, but the annotation/evaluation pipeline is YOLO-native and less aligned with the COCO master + MMDetection SSOD protocol. The teacher-student SSOD pipeline and No Finding empty-image handling would require more project-specific adaptation. Rejected as primary framework.

Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.object_detection_support: torchvision provides detection models, but the training/eval stack is ours to build
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.ssod_teacher_student_readiness: none: EMA teacher, strong/weak augmentation branches, and the pseudo-label loop must all be implemented
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.config_reproducibility: must design a config/experiment protocol ourselves
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.empty_no_finding_image_handling: fully under our control, but every guarantee is also ours to test
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.implementation_burden: high: custom dataset, dataloader, evaluator, trainer, pseudo-label loop, EMA teacher, COCO metric integration, logging and config protocol
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.research_reproducibility: low-medium: bespoke code is harder for others to reproduce or compare against published baselines
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.fit_for_this_thesis: poor: engineering effort and silent-bug risk would dominate the research contribution
Custom_PyTorch_torchvision.rejection_reason: Maximum flexibility, but requires custom dataset, dataloader, evaluator, trainer, pseudo-label loop, EMA teacher, COCO metric integration, logging and config protocol. High implementation risk and reproducibility risk.

framework_selection_conclusion: MMDetection is selected as the primary framework because it best matches the planned COCO-based teacher-student SSOD workflow, supports COCO-style evaluation, offers config-driven reproducibility, and reduces the amount of custom training/evaluation code required. Detectron2 remains an optional fallback only after GPT re-review.
category_id_policy: COCO category_id is a contiguous integer 1..14 (No Finding excluded). canonical_class_id (0..13) and class_id_original are preserved in category metadata for traceability.
image_path_policy: COCO file_name uses relative_dicom_path; resolved at load time by joining the VINBIGDATA_DICOM_ROOT root.
